lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay, let's get started. Today we need to agree on the release plan for version three of the mobile app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thanks. From the backend side, the new sync API is feature complete, but load testing is only half done.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: On the design side, we still have two screens waiting for accessibility review. Contrast on the dark theme failed in a couple of places.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: Quality assurance found eleven open bugs, three of them are crashes on older Android devices.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three crashes is a lot. Are those blockers for the release, or can we ship with a known issues list?

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: Two of them are blockers. They happen during login, so a user could not get into the app at all.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I looked at one of them yesterday. It is a race condition when the token refresh and the profile request run at the same time.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: Is that the same issue we saw in the beta last month, the one with the blank profile picture?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Related, but not identical. The profile picture bug was a caching problem. This one is in the authentication layer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How long would a proper fix take, including tests?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Probably three days for the fix and another two for regression testing on the device farm.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: The device farm is booked by the payments team next Tuesday and Wednesday, so we should reserve it early.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good point. I will talk to their manager today and ask for Thursday and Friday instead.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: While we are on scheduling, the marketing team wants screenshots of the new onboarding flow by the end of next week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can we give them screenshots before the accessibility review is finished?

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: We can, but the colors might change slightly. I would label them as preliminary.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: Please also include the tablet layouts. Last time the store listing only showed phone screenshots and we got complaints.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Speaking of tablets, the sync API returns larger pages on tablets. That doubled the memory use in one of our tests.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is that a problem for the release, or just something to optimize later?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For the release it is acceptable. Memory stays under the limit, but I would like to cap the page size in the next version.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: I can add a test case that measures memory on the smallest supported tablet so we notice regressions.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: One more design question. Do we keep the old navigation bar for users who upgrade, or switch everyone to the new one?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My preference is to switch everyone, but show a short tour the first time they open the app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A tour means one more remote configuration flag. That is fine, but it needs a default value if the configuration service is down.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: And we should test the tour with the screen reader. Tours are often a nightmare for accessibility.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: Agreed. I will make sure every step of the tour has proper labels and can be skipped.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let's talk about the rollout. Do we do a staged rollout on both stores?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On Android we can do five percent, then twenty, then everyone. Apple's phased release is similar but takes seven days.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: During the staged rollout I want crash reporting dashboards visible to the whole team, not just to engineering.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That is reasonable. Who owns the decision to halt the rollout if crashes go up?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The on-call engineer should be able to halt it immediately, and then inform the rest of us.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: Can we define a threshold, like a crash-free rate below ninety nine point five percent?

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: Ninety nine point five sounds right. Our current version sits at ninety nine point eight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay, so the threshold is ninety nine point five, and the on-call engineer can halt. I will write that down.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One risk I want to mention: the payment provider is changing their SDK next month, and we have not tested the beta yet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does that affect version three, or only the release after it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Only the release after it, as long as we ship version three before the end of the month.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: Then the date really matters. If we slip by two weeks, we would have to integrate the new SDK first.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: From the testing side, two weeks of slip is realistic if the login crash takes longer than expected.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the login crash is on the critical path. Let's make that the top priority for the backend team this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fine with me. I will pair with someone from the mobile team so we fix both sides of the race.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: I can free up some time to help with the error messages on the login screen, they are confusing right now.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: And I will retest the other nine bugs on Monday to see which ones are already fixed by the recent merges.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. Let me summarize. Login crash first, device farm on Thursday and Friday, preliminary screenshots for marketing, staged rollout with a ninety nine point five threshold.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sounds right. I will post the technical plan for the race condition fix in the channel this afternoon.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: I will send the accessibility review dates once I have confirmed them with the external auditor.

lines.speaker: D
lines.text: And I will share the updated bug list after Monday's retest. Thanks everyone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thanks all, see you on Thursday for the follow-up.
